purpose: Replace the existing six-identity Studio directional walking artwork with clearer native silhouettes and visible alternating limbs
layout_note: The delivered sheet contains twelve columns and six rows. Actual transparent gutters were reviewed at alpha >= 160: rows [55,187], [201,336], [355,487], [510,647], [665,806], [832,962]. Nominal 160-pixel row boundaries would clip the blond and robot silhouettes; the compiler uses the reviewed bounds recorded in ../directional.json.

references.role: sole edit reference; prior committed six-identity directional source

prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production sprite artwork for the existing Agent Office canvas app. Improve the supplied existing sprite sheet while preserving exactly its six character identities, outfits, palettes and cozy pixel-art style. The result will be normalized to 32 by 36 logical pixels per character. Draw clean, intentional pixel clusters, readable dark-navy outlines, simple expressive faces, crisp opaque colors and true transparent space. No gradients, grain, fuzzy antialias halos, glows, outlines around the whole sheet, background colors, scenery, ground, shadows, desks, text, labels, logos or grid lines.

Canvas: 1536 by 1024 pixels. EXACTLY twelve equal columns and six equal rows of isolated full-body sprites: 72 sprites total, not a poster. Use 128 by 160 pixel slots with 32px top and bottom outer margins. Each character stays entirely inside its slot with generous transparent gutters. All poses of one identity share the same head size, body proportions, costume details and foot baseline; feet are at the same y position within each slot. Treat this as crisp 32x36 game pixel art enlarged for production, with large readable color clusters rather than tiny decoration.

Rows, top to bottom, are the same existing six identities: (1) tousled brown hair, navy jacket/trousers, pale shirt and cyan tie; (2) copper-orange ponytail, teal jacket, pale blouse, dark trousers; (3) indigo hair and dark rectangular glasses, navy outfit with violet tie; (4) blond tousled hair, saturated blue hoodie and dark trousers—keep this blue clothing so existing rose/moss palette variants work; (5) compact ivory office robot, dark visor with two cyan rectangular eyes, cyan antenna tip, navy joints and feet; (6) warm dark skin, red cap, red jacket over pale shirt, dark trousers. Maintain the same character designs across all 12 cells in their row.

WALK SHEET: replace the existing directional walk sheet with stronger, clearly distinct but restrained walk poses. In EVERY row, columns 1–3 face DOWN toward viewer; columns 4–6 face UP away from viewer with back of head and NO face; columns 7–9 face RIGHT in a clear side profile; columns 10–12 face LEFT in a clear side profile. Within each direction the three poses are: neutral balanced stance, left foot forward with opposite arm forward, right foot forward with opposite arm forward. The foot separation and arm swing must remain visible after downsampling to 32x36. Keep heads stable in height and width, avoid body-size changes or stretching. The robot follows the same heading and alternating-leg pattern. Each pose is a separate upright full-body figure. Match the supplied identities, improve silhouette clarity and direction readability. Genuine transparent RGBA background.
normalization: Reviewed alpha >= 160 crop bounds; one shared scale per identity across all twelve poses; nearest-neighbor sampling; 32 x 36 native frames with bottom-center anchor (16, 35). Generated source bytes remain unmodified.
